title: Zanzibar New Year Feast
community: Makunduchi, Zanzibar — the Shirazi New Year celebration
author: Chef Fatuma

heritage.origin: Makunduchi, southern Zanzibar — the Shirazi Persian New Year celebration
heritage.history: Mwaka Kogwa is Zanzibar's most ancient celebration — the Shirazi Persian New Year observed in the village of Makunduchi each July. Men engage in symbolic battles with banana stalks to settle the year's grievances; women parade through the village in their finest kanga cloth. The feast that follows is the greatest meal of the Zanzibar year — pilau, biriani, grilled meats, coconut sweets, and the full expression of the island's food culture.

desc: Zanzibar Mwaka Kogwa Feast — the menu of Zanzibar's most ancient celebration: Zanzibar Pilau, Biriani, Nyama Choma, Halwa, Kashata, and the full array of Swahili coast dishes. A guide to assembling the complete Zanzibar celebration feast for the most important occasions.
longDesc: The Mwaka Kogwa feast represents the complete Zanzibar food tradition assembled for the most important occasion of the year. This recipe is really a menu guide — showing how to combine the individual dishes into a coherent celebration feast. The centrepiece is always the pilau or biriani; the accompaniments include grilled meats, coastal salads, sweet coconut confections, and the universal pili pili.
ingredients: Zanzibar Biryani (TZA121) — for the grandest tables
Nyama Choma / Goat Roast (TZA035) — grilled celebration meat
Samaki wa Kupaka (TZA061) — coconut basted fish
Halwa ya Zanzibar (TZA147) — the celebration sweet
equipment: Everything — this is a full day's cooking
steps: Day before: marinate meats for pilau and biriani. Make halwa. Fry onions for layering.
Morning of feast: begin the pilau or biriani base. Prepare goat for roasting.
Midday: assemble and dum the biriani/pilau. Begin goat roast over charcoal.
Two hours before serving: prepare kachumbari, chatni, pili pili, and kashata.
One hour before: begin samaki wa kupaka grilling.
Final hour: complete all components. Assemble the feast table.
Break the biriani dum seal at the table — the ceremony that signals the feast begins.
chefTips: See individual recipes for all detailed techniques.
A feast this size requires a team — cooking alone for 20+ is not Zanzibari practice.
The biriani seal must be broken at the table — the fragrance release is the ceremony.
Prepare the sweets the day before — they improve overnight.

sustainabilityTips: The communal cooking model of Mwaka Kogwa is inherently sustainable — shared resources, shared labour, shared celebration.
servedWith: The feast is complete — everything is served together

healthBenefits: A celebration feast — eaten with joy and shared with generosity.
culturalNote: Mwaka Kogwa is Zanzibar's most ancient celebration and its food is the most complete expression of what the island's cooking tradition can produce. To attend Mwaka Kogwa and eat at the feast table in Makunduchi is to experience Zanzibar at its most joyful, most generous, and most fully itself.
